about.body: I build websites for local businesses: the barbershop, the restaurant and the studio down the street. Every site is written in code and designed for that business, no templates, so it's fast, looks great on every screen and brings you inquiries.

points.title: What I build
points.text: Business websites and landing pages for local businesses: a page that shows off your business, services, opening hours and location, with a WhatsApp button and a contact form.

points.title: My tools
points.text: Next.js, React and Tailwind CSS, the same tech big companies use. I also use AI tools to build faster, and every line of code goes through me and gets tested before it goes live.

points.title: How I work
points.text: Directly with you on WhatsApp, no middlemen. Mobile-first, built to the Israeli accessibility standard, with the privacy policy and accessibility statement the law asks for.

points.title: What you get
points.text: A fast site that's ready for Google, looks great on every screen and makes it easy for customers to reach you. Once it's paid in full, the site and its content are yours.

process.title: How it works
process.intro: Four steps from the first message to a live site. You see every stage, and nothing goes live without your OK.

steps.title: We talk on WhatsApp
steps.text: Send me a message and tell me about your business and what matters to you. No long forms, no pointless meetings.

steps.title: I build a demo
steps.text: I put together a first version of your site, so you can see how it'll actually look instead of imagining it.

steps.title: You approve it
steps.text: We go through the demo together and fix whatever needs fixing: colors, text, photos. We only move on when you're happy.

steps.title: Your site goes live
steps.text: I connect your domain, check that everything works on phones and computers, and your customers can find you.

faq.title: Questions I get asked
faq.intro: Didn't find your answer? Send me a message, I'm happy to answer anything.

items.q: How long does it take to build a website?
items.a: Usually somewhere between a few days and two weeks. A one-page site is ready faster; a site with several pages and more content takes longer. A lot also depends on how quickly I get your content and approvals. On our first call I'll give you an estimate for your site.

It depends on the site: how many pages, which features and how much content it needs. There's no fixed price list, so the easiest thing is to tell me what you need and I'll get back to you with a quote. The call and the quote are free, no strings attached.

items.q: What do I need to prepare?
items.a: Your logo, if you have one. Some text about your business and services, photos (of the place, your products or your team), opening hours and contact details. No text ready? That's fine, I can help you write it.

items.q: Will the site work well on phones?
items.a: Yes. I build every site for phones first and only then adapt it for computers, because most of your customers will come from their phone. Before the site goes live, I test it on screens of different sizes.

items.q: Is the site accessible, as Israeli law requires?
items.a: I build sites to the Israeli accessibility standard IS 5568 and the WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines: keyboard navigation, color contrast, descriptions for screen readers and more. Accessibility is built into the code itself, not added with a plugin, and every site comes with an accessibility statement.

items.q: What happens after the site goes live?
items.a: Your site is live and working. If you'd like, you can add monthly maintenance: updates, small changes like prices or opening hours, and keeping an eye on the site to make sure it's up and running. It's optional; you can also just reach out whenever you need something.
Yes. Once it's paid in full, the site and its content belong to you.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: What information Isaac's website collects, why, where it goes, and how to see, correct or delete it.

blocks.p: Your privacy matters to me. This page explains, in plain language, what information is collected when you contact me through this site, what I do with it, and what your rights are.
This site is run by {name}, an independent web developer. For any privacy question, email me at {email} or call {phone}.
The site only collects what you choose to fill in on the contact form:

ul: Full name
Phone number
Email address (optional)
The message you write

blocks.p: You're not legally required to give these details, but without a name and a way to reach you, I can't get back to you. Please don't include sensitive information the inquiry doesn't need.

Only to get back to you about your inquiry. It isn't used for marketing or newsletters, it isn't sold, and it isn't shared with anyone except the service that delivers the message to me (details below).

blocks.h2: Where it goes and where it's stored

blocks.p: When you send the form, your details go through Web3Forms, an outside form-delivery service, to my email inbox. The servers of that service and of my email provider (Gmail) may be located outside Israel.

The site itself doesn't store your details: there's no database, no files are saved, and no logs with personal information are kept. The message is kept only in my inbox, for as long as it's needed to handle your inquiry.
If you contact me on WhatsApp, by phone or by email instead, the information passes through those services and their privacy policies apply too.
The site doesn't use analytics tools or tracking pixels, and doesn't load content from third-party sites while you browse. Fonts are served from this site.

The site saves only two preferences in your browser so they stick for your next visit: the language you picked (in a cookie called locale) and whether you paused animations (in localStorage). They're never sent to me and aren't used for tracking.
Like any website, the hosting provider (Vercel) may log basic technical data, such as your IP address and browser type, for security and to run the server.
Under Israel's Privacy Protection Law, you can at any time:

ul: Ask to see the information stored about you
Ask to correct information that's wrong
Ask to delete the information

blocks.p: To do any of these, email {email} or call {phone}. I'll handle your request within 30 days at most.

The site uses an encrypted connection (HTTPS), and the form is protected against spam. Still, no way of sending data over the internet is 100% secure, so please don't send sensitive information through the form.
If this policy changes, the updated version will be posted on this page with a new date.

accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.description: The accessibility statement for Isaac's website: the standard it follows, what was made accessible, known limitations, and how to report an accessibility issue.

blocks.p: I want everyone to be able to use this site, including people with disabilities. Accessibility was planned in from the start and is built into the code itself, with no add-on or "accessibility widget".

The site was built to the Israeli Standard ת״י 5568 (IS 5568) and the WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines, as required by Israel's Equal Rights for Persons with Disabilities regulations (accessibility adjustments for services).

ul: Full keyboard navigation (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and Esc), in an order that follows the reading direction.
A "Skip to content" link at the start of every page, and a clear focus outline on everything you can interact with.
A heading and landmark structure (header, navigation, main content, footer) that screen readers recognize.
Color contrast of at least 4.5:1 for regular text and 3:1 for large text, form fields and icons.
The mobile menu moves focus inside, closes with Esc, and returns focus to the button that opened it.

A pause/play button (⏸/▶) on the moving orange band on the home page, and a "Stop animations" option in the accessibility menu on every page. Both stop all motion that plays on its own, and your choice is saved for your next visit.
Respect for your system's "reduce motion" setting: movement is replaced with gentle fades.
In the contact form: a visible label for every field, "(required)" written out in words, and clear error messages that screen readers announce.
Frequently asked questions in an accessible accordion that opens and closes with the keyboard.
The site is available in Hebrew and English, with the right language and reading direction set for each.
Icon-only buttons and links have a text description, and links that open in a new window say so.
The site works at 200% zoom and at a screen width of 320 pixels with no sideways scrolling.
Touch targets are at least 44×44 pixels.

blocks.p: In the corner of the screen there's a small accessibility menu, built into the site rather than added by a third-party plugin. It lets you make the text bigger (100%, 115% or 130%), turn on high contrast, highlight links, switch to a more readable font and stop animations. Your choices are saved in your browser for your next visit.
The menu is a supplementary tool only. The site's accessibility is built into the code itself, and the site meets the requirements without using the menu.
The site was tested with the automated checker axe, a manual keyboard-only pass, in "reduce motion" mode, and on screens 1440, 768, 390 and 320 pixels wide, in Chrome.

ul: The phone-screen illustrations are for show only, so they're hidden from screen readers. Everything they show is also written in the text next to them.
A full test with screen readers (like NVDA or VoiceOver) hasn't been done yet. If you run into a problem, I'd like to hear about it and fix it.

blocks.h2: Found a problem? Let me know

blocks.p: If something on the site isn't accessible to you, or you have a suggestion, contact the accessibility coordinator, {name}:

ul: Email: {email}
Phone: {phone}

blocks.p: To help me fix it, tell me which page the problem was on, what you were trying to do, and which browser or assistive technology you used. I'll get back to you soon.
